# MuJoCo Roadster Stunt Simulation: Trajectory Optimization and Closed Loop Control

How does a car use jet thrust to perform aerial flips, landings, and ramp driving? This section introduces [Khai Nguyen’s open-source Roadster stunt project ](https://github.com/xkhainguyen/roadster-stunt). From preview and environment installation to planning, simulation, and result inspection, it explains how trajectory optimization and feedback control work together.

## The Relationship between Videos and Projects

[ Kevin Zakka's MuJoCo Roadster video ](https://x.com/kevin_zakka/status/2112051258635042823) shows the Roadster stunts. He explains how to use the MuJoCo site actuator to simulate nozzles, the adhesion actuator to simulate slope adsorption, and box QP to distribute jet thrust. No public source code for this video has been found so far.

The [roadster-stunt](https://github.com/xkhainguyen/roadster-stunt) introduced in this tutorial is independently implemented by **Khai Nguyen**. It also uses MuJoCo to reproduce Roadster flips and ramp actions, along with demonstrations of it falling onto moving trucks. Its algorithm and scenarios belong to another implementation. The project uses the [MIT license](https://github.com/xkhainguyen/roadster-stunt/blob/a726d1a23ee1954d7376e6e48cc7c4460fd3ac4f/LICENSE); the following animated GIFs are directly from the project's demonstration files. The vehicle and control parameters are estimated by the project's author.

## How the control system works

The project represents the car as a MuJoCo model with a suspension, jet propulsion, and limited air source. The author divides the trajectory and control into three parts:

1. **Offline planning**: Use CasADi and IPOPT to optimize the flight trajectory and thrust timing, generating reference actions.
2. **Aerial attitude correction**: Run LQR at 100 Hz to adjust control based on the deviation between actual and reference attitudes.
3. **Landing control**: Run the TinyMPC model predictive controller at 50 Hz to calculate landing control during approach to the ground.

The planning provides an expected trajectory, while feedback control corrects the actual motion when model errors or external disturbances occur. In the ramp example, the author simulates vehicle adhesion using a constant suction force; the suction force parameter given in the upstream README is 20 kN, which is the setting for this simulation model.

The author reported a disturbance example in the upstream README: the vehicle mass increased by 4%, the nozzle thrust decreased by 3%, and a gust was applied during the flip; when only the scheduled jet timing was replayed, the touchdown speed was 8 m/s, while after adding feedback, it became 0.9 m/s. These are the results under a single setting reported by the upstream project, and this repository has not been retested yet.

## Installation and Execution

The following steps are fixed to the upstream submission [[`a726d1a`](https://github.com/xkhainguyen/roadster-stunt/tree/a726d1a23ee1954d7376e6e48cc7c4460fd3ac4f). Git, Conda, or a compatible environment manager is required; the project environment file specifies dependencies such as Python 3.11, MuJoCo, CasADi, and TinyMPC. The first installation involves downloading dependencies and models, and the actual time depends on the network.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/xkhainguyen/roadster-stunt.git
cd roadster-stunt
git checkout a726d1a23ee1954d7376e6e48cc7c4460fd3ac4f
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate roadster
pip install -e .
```

Run flip and ramp experiments:

```bash
python scripts/run_kickflip.py
python scripts/run_ramp.py
```

The two scripts traverse the scene and open/closed loop modes respectively, save the `.npz` log in `data/`, and output metrics such as landing speed and attitude error. Run the test according to the upstream instructions:

```bash
MUJOCO_GL=egl pytest
```

`MUJOCO_GL=egl` is an upstream no-window rendering example that requires the environment to have available EGL support. Video generation requires additional video and audio dependencies. For commands and output locations, see [ upstream README ](https://github.com/xkhainguyen/roadster-stunt/tree/a726d1a23ee1954d7376e6e48cc7c4460fd3ac4f); the example animated GIF can be viewed directly on this page. The commands in this section have been verified with the upstream source code, but have not been actually run in this repository yet.
